text:
kevin: quick question — we keep getting tenant complaints when audit export webhooks time out. Do we: 1) ACK immediately with a delivery_id and do async retries (so UX shows success), or 2) block and surface failure to console and count it against export quota? need to pick a pattern for compliance exports.

sophia: ack-then-retry is nicer for caller apps but makes quota semantics fuzzy. if we ack and later fail permanently, how do we bill?

maria: +1 to ack-then-retry, but we must have a clear "final_state" in the export UI and webhook callbacks (delivered|failed). otherwise customers can't prove delivery for audits.

josh: what if we split billing: decrement quota at enqueue time, but expose delivery outcome telemetry and a refund pathway for permanent failures?

anna: refund pathways are messy for committed capacity customers (dedicated). for hosted customers quota = metered tokens; we can credit, but dedicated reserved capacity expects predictable consumption.

kevin: good point. the thread is specifically about "compliance export" (downloadable ndjson / webhooks). dedicated tenants also request signed proofs of delivery. we need a single behavior with flags.

maria: proposal: default = ack-on-accept (return delivery_id). billing happens at accept. provide explicit final webhook callback with failure reason if retries exhausted. Console shows "accepted -> delivering -> delivered|failed" timeline and includes signed proof when delivered. For dedicated, an option "synchronous_delivery=true" to block and return final status (and bill only on delivered).

sophia: that seems sane. two small concerns: 1) telemetry — we need to emit events for each state so we can alert/regress, 2) rate-limiting/backpressure — if endpoint is slow, we should throttle per-tenant retries to avoid herd effects.

josh: +1 on telemetry. suggest emitting these events: export.accept, export.enqueue, export.retry, export.final (with status). Also attach actor_id, tenant_id, export_id, delivery_id, attempt_count.

kevin: sample event payload that ops wants: 
```
{
  "event": "export.final",
  "export_id": "exp_01F...",
  "delivery_id": "del_83A...",
  "tenant_id": "t-42",
  "status": "failed",
  "reason": "http_504",
  "attempts": 5
}
```

anna: perfect. also need a metric (per-tenant) for in-flight webhook deliveries and a throttling config per tenant. SLO=95% final success within 10m? open to numbers.

kevin: ops ask: how should console show failures for compliance owners? immediate red flag with ability to download signed failure report. we also need an export retry log downloadable for compliance.

maria: console wire: in exports list show a small state machine pill and a link "view delivery proof". If failed, show last error, attempts, next retry ETA and a button "manually resend" (only available to tenant admins).

sophia: API detail: when we ACK we return: 
```
200 OK
{
  "delivery_id": "del_83A...",
  "export_id": "exp_01F...",
  "status": "accepted"
}
```
Later final callback POST to customer's webhook: 
```
POST /customer/webhook
{
  "delivery_id": "del_83A...",
  "export_id": "exp_01F...",
  "status": "delivered",
  "signed_proof": "<base64sig>"
}
```

josh: note: signed_proof only generated when using our delivery pipeline to origin (we sign the envelope). For direct S3 uploads we return a signed upload URL and proof is a signed manifest. need to call that out in docs.

devops-bot: new deploy: export-worker v3.2 -> includes per-tenant retry queues and backoff. monitor: aws/sqs-retry-lag.

kevin: backlog/action items: 
- implement telemetry events (sophia/josh)
- console delivery timeline + manual resend (maria)
- API + docs: ack payload + final callback spec (sophia)
- billing behavior: default bill-on-accept, "synchronous_delivery" flag for dedicated (anna)
- per-tenant throttle config + SLOs (anna/devops)

anna: i'll pair with finance on billing edge cases for dedicated tenants. we should define refund SLAs in contract language.

maria: UX question — do we expose retry policy details in console or hide behind advanced config? my vote: hide by default, surface only next retry ETA and attempt_count. keep it simple.

sophia: agree. expose full retry logs in a download for compliance only.

josh: one more: telemetry retention for these events needs to be longer for compliance tenants (12 months). do we want an opt-in/storage tier?

kevin: yes. add an opt-in retention tier to the billing add-on. compliance customers can request 12-24 month retention.

compliance-bot: note: any change must include an audit trail of who changed retry/throttle configs. ensure config changes produce an auditable change event.

kevin: thanks — will write up RFC with the proposal and the API samples above. pinging @maria @sophia @anna for reviews. :thumbsup:
